comment.narrative: A Benguela Current Commission has been formally adopted as has a Benguela Current Convention. The BCC needs to be more appropriately structured and supported and needs stronger institutional and intersectoral representation at the national level. Both the BCC Implementation Plan and the Convention expectations need to be harmonised under one set of priorities and these need to drive and deliver actual stress reduction activities. Stronger stakeholder engagement in this process is essential for the long term management of LME resources as is a long-term investment plan to support stress reduction improvements.

1. National validation workshops for the three guidelines to be conducted in Q1 of 2022.
2. Demonstration projects completed. Indicators: (1) Namibia: Blue Economy Policy validated (2) Angola: Ocean Strategy validated; mussel culture structure monitoring & assessment of structure components and elements designed and implemented; (3) South Africa: Develop management plans for two (2) Marine Protected Areas.
3. National Action Plans (NAPs) adopted by all three countries.
4. Sustainable long-term management structures and financing mechanisms in place.

1. Following finalization of Governance Baseline Assessment in 2019. BCC through its BCLME III Project contracted a consultancy to develop guidelines for Oil and Gas Exploration/Development, Prospecting and Mining of the Seabed, and Waste Management and Discharges of Plastic into the Ocean. National consultations have been convened in all member states to review the draft guidelines and the final validation workshop was held in August 2022.
2. Demonstration projects:
(1) Namibia: Blue Economy Policy - A National Technical Inter-Ministerial Committee on Blue Economy has been supported to develop Namibia’s Blue Economy Policy. The draft policy has been produced, however, has not been submitted for Cabinet endorsement as yet.
(2) Angola: (1) A demonstration focusing on small-scale community level mariculture of bivalves in coastal communities in the Benguela Province, Angola resulted in the construction of the mussel productions infrastructure of approximately 3kg per meter of ropes, which translates to a total of 90kg of mussels was completed. Infrastructure monitoring is continuously carried out on a monthly basis, which assesses mussel growth and quality of nutrients at the farming site. (2) The Ocean Strategy was not validated
(3) South Africa: Develop management plans for two (2) Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) - Estuary rehabilitation and MPA management capacity development in South Africa.
3. BCC National Action Plans (NAPs) adopted by all three countries - A NAP validation for Namibia was held in July 2022 after the submission of the draft consultancy report in May 2022. The project supported the establishment and operations of National Inter-sectoral Coordinating (NICs) structures for national Convention domestication and SAP implementation. Including sector integrated structures for development of Strategy for the Seas in Angola and the Blue Economy policy in Namibia. NICs serve as structures promoting Science-to-Governance and supported NAPs development.
4. Sustainable long-term management structures and financing mechanisms in place - Deferred to 2023 for completion.
Additional Activities in 2022 • Governance Baseline Assessment (GBA) completed • SAP 2015–2019 implementation progress reviewed and assessed • Protocols/standards/guidelines on four priority areas arising from GBA adopted • TDA update finalized • Identification of suitable/relevant regional policy and management platforms that will influence ocean governance of the BCLME at the regional level, to which scientific information should be fed in a strategic and systematic manner • Status report on legal and institutional arrangements as well as the implementation of measures (e.g. on ballast water management, IUU fishing, oil spill response, etc.) • Partnership agreements adopted and signed for sustainable fisheries (eco-labelling) in the BCLME • Contribute towards the full ratification of the Ballast Water Management Convention by Namibia and South Africa • Biodiversity inventory report • “Fit-for-purpose” water quality standards established for the demonstration site • A set of water quality monitoring indicators agreed • An organisational performance review finalised and areas requiring strengthening identified • Capacity needs assessment conducted

1. Three draft guidelines produced for (1) oil and gas exploration; (2) prospecting and mining of the seabed; (3) management and discharges of waste and plastics and submitted to the BCC for review.
2. Demonstration project progress update: (a) Namibia: Blue Economy Policy drafted (not yet validated). 700 citizens consulted between 1st - 8th October 2021; groundwork completed for constructing a fish shop and economic development and technical support to artisanal fishers along the Namibian west coast. (b) Angola: Phase 1 structures put in place for mussel production in Coata, Benguela; 35 women trained on model 1 and 2 for mussel processing; marine species book finalised and published; first draft of Ocean Strategy completed. (c) South Africa: A number of activities took place at the Swartkops Estuary, including installation of floating wetlands, construction of filtration traps at identified pollution hotspots etc. There is interest to expand and replicate the experiences at Swartkops Estuary to similar strained ecosystems.
3. Significant progress has been made towards establishing national coordinating structures for the domestication of the SAP. The South African National Inter-Sectoral Committee (NICC) launched and met every quarter in 2021. The Namibian National Inter-sectoral Committee on Ocean Governance (NISCOG) is also active in the coordination and governance of the Namibian national activities. Angola has resolved to strengthen the existing national Ecosystem Advisory Committee so that it fulfils the role of inter-sectoral coordination.
4. Transboundary Diagnostic Analysis finalised in 2021.
